Limerick won the most recent All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final, defeating Galway. Limerick won the match on a scoreline of 1–29 to 1–11, it was their sixth All-Ireland title since 2018.

The match was played at Croke Park in Dublin on 19 July 2026. Limerick defeated Galway in the final in Croke Park. This was their last title being in 2023, when they completed a four-in-a-row, making this their latest crown in an era of dominance.

The most recent All-Ireland senior hurling final was played on **19 July 2026** at Croke Park, between **Limerick** and **Galway**.

Limerick won the match on a scoreline of 1–29 to 1–11, marking their sixth All-Ireland title since 2018. (Note: some sources, including Munster GAA's report, list the final score slightly differently — as Limerick defeating Galway by 1-29 to 1-18 — but all confirm Limerick's decisive victory.)

This win gave Limerick their **13th All-Ireland title overall**, with Cian Lynch as captain and John Kiely as manager, extending their dominant run in modern hurling.
